claim.value: A chronology that appears complete may incorrectly join records of different orders.
claim.scope: A possible identity error despite apparent chronological completeness.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly identifies joining different orders as a possible defect in a complete-looking chronology.

signal_basis.value: Cross-check order identifiers and transaction details across records and reconstruct their sequence; mismatched identities and missing links signal uncertainty.
signal_basis.scope: Proposed checks of individual order histories, evaluated assuming execution and the described signal; no actual mismatch is asserted.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply identity cross-checking, sequence reconstruction, identity discrepancies as uncertainty signals, and the checks' prospective status.
No unresolved empirical relation is needed for this supported possibility claim.

rationale: Chronological completeness does not establish that every linked record concerns the same order. The operation distinguishes identity checks from sequence reconstruction, licensing the bounded possibility of an identity error without establishing that one actually occurred.
uncertainty: Whether any particular reconstructed chronology joins different orders remains undetermined; the claim asserts only that this can happen.
